title: AI Engineer Roadmap: 28 Weeks (Python-First, Go and Rust Where Production Demands)

sections.label: Fundamental
items: LLM API mechanics: tokens, context windows, sampling, streaming, cost model.
Structured outputs and JSON-schema validation.
Python async programming (asyncio, timeouts, cancellation, backpressure) and strict typing with Pydantic.
Git workflow (trunk-based, PR checks) and Linux basics for running services (processes, ports, logs).
Resilience patterns: timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breaker.

sections.label: Targets
items: A provider-agnostic gateway that treats model output as untrusted input.
Failure behaviour defined before features.

sections.label: Implement
items: FastAPI service with a provider interface (Protocol or ABC) and adapters (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini), fully typed and checked with mypy or pyright.
Project tooling: uv or poetry, ruff, pre-commit, pytest.
Schema-validated structured outputs with bounded retries and repair prompts.
REST endpoints (plus one gRPC endpoint via grpcio), streaming over SSE, config-driven provider selection, rate limits.
Dockerfile, GitHub Actions pipeline, unit tests with injected failures (timeouts, malformed JSON).
Run the service on a Linux host or VM with systemd and log inspection, not only on your laptop.
Create the eval package inside the same repo (pytest, dataset folder) so services and evals share types.

sections.label: Practical project
items: `ai-chassis` repo. First use case: extract fields from synthetic bank statements and loan documents into a typed schema.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Python microservices (FastAPI) over REST and gRPC; model-agnostic abstraction; failure modes, retries and guardrails; async API design.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Switching provider requires a config change only, no caller change.
Malformed model output is rejected or repaired, never passed through.
Failure-injection tests pass in CI.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Repo with README, architecture diagram, passing CI.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Embeddings, chunking strategies, HNSW indexes in pgvector.
Kafka semantics: at-least-once delivery, idempotent consumers, consumer groups, replay.
OpenTelemetry basics.

sections.label: Targets
items: A deployed end-to-end skeleton with citations and traces from day one.

sections.label: Implement
items: Ingest events on Kafka, chunk, embed and write to pgvector (Python consumers, for example confluent-kafka).
Retrieval plus generation endpoint returning answers with chunk-level citations.
OpenTelemetry tracing and a trace per request.
Write 40 golden Q&A cases and a first eval script in Python.
Deploy to your chosen cloud.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Policy Q&A over about 30 public regulatory and policy documents (KYC/AML guidance, lending rules).

sections.label: Production mapping
items: RAG over internal documents; Kafka/CDC pipelines; observability.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Replaying the event stream creates no duplicate chunks.
Every answer carries citations that resolve to stored chunks.
Live URL, a trace per request, and a recorded baseline score.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Deployed v0 and a baseline eval report (scores, failure examples).

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Hybrid search (full-text plus vector), reranking, query rewriting.
Metrics: recall@k, MRR; latency budgets.
Postgres indexing, `EXPLAIN`, Redis caching and invalidation.

sections.label: Targets
items: Retrieval decisions justified with numbers, within a latency budget.

sections.label: Implement
items: Three or more retrieval configurations: vector only, hybrid, hybrid plus reranker.
Chunking and metadata experiments.
Redis cache with **permission-aware keys**.
Query and index tuning pass using `EXPLAIN`.
Replicate the core schema and three key queries on MySQL; compare indexing behaviour, `EXPLAIN` output and transactional differences with PostgreSQL.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Retrieval comparison report on the policy corpus.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Hybrid retrieval, reranking, pgvector, PostgreSQL tuning, Redis, latency and cost control.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Report compares at least three configurations with recall@k, MRR and p95 latency; the chosen one is justified.
A test proves one user cannot receive another user's cached result.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Retrieval report, tuned schema and indexes. **CV v1 and first batch of low-stakes applications sent.**

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Eval set design, error analysis, failure taxonomies.
LLM-as-judge: calibration against human labels, bias, noise.
Regression testing for non-deterministic systems.

sections.label: Targets
items: The eval harness becomes a release gate.

sections.label: Implement
items: Grow to 100+ cases across normal, edge and adversarial inputs.
Label a subset yourself and measure judge agreement.
Regression tracking across prompt, model and retrieval changes.
CI gate and a dashboard for quality, latency and cost per run.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Eval-first pipeline for the policy Q&A service.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Evaluation in every AI feature; monitoring quality, latency and cost; measure-first mindset.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: A deliberately degraded prompt fails CI.
Judge-versus-human agreement is measured and reported (set a threshold, for example 80%, and document the actual figure).
Failure taxonomy covers every observed failure in the set.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Eval report, taxonomy document, CI gate.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Tool-calling contracts, ReAct, plan-and-execute.
State, checkpoints, idempotency, human-in-the-loop approval.
Agent failure modes: loops, wrong tool, runaway cost.

sections.label: Targets
items: An agent that is bounded, auditable and measurable.

sections.label: Implement
items: Python agent loop written from scratch (asyncio, typed tool contracts).
Tools: customer lookup, transaction search, draft case note (mock banking API).
Step and cost limits, per-tool permission scopes, idempotent actions.
Approval gate for any write action.
Trajectory evals (tool-call accuracy, task success).
Side exercise (half a day): rebuild one flow in LangGraph and read LangChain's tool abstractions, so you can discuss the frameworks the JDs name.

sections.label: Practical project
items: KYC case assistant: investigate a flagged customer, cite policy, draft a case note for human approval.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Agentic workflows with tool calling; at least one major framework; approval gates for high-risk actions.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: The agent halts at its step and cost limits.
Write actions cannot execute without approval (tested).
Tool-call accuracy and task success measured on 30+ scenarios.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Agent module, trajectory eval results, short design note comparing hand-rolled and LangGraph versions.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Model Context Protocol: tools, resources, transport.
Supervisor-worker patterns, context sharing.
Short-term versus long-term memory: what to store, retrieve and expire.

sections.label: Targets
items: Your tools usable by any MCP client; evidence on whether multi-agent helps.

sections.label: Implement
items: MCP server exposing your tools (use the official Python MCP SDK; check its current version and transport support first).
Supervisor plus worker agents built in LangGraph, then re-implemented in CrewAI with the same tools and eval set to compare orchestration styles (note AutoGen as a third option).
Memory store in Postgres with TTL, summarization and retrieval.
A/B comparison: single agent versus multi-agent.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Extend the KYC assistant with persisted case memory and a supervisor that delegates retrieval and drafting.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: MCP, multi-agent systems, context layer and memory (security JD, AI-backend JD).

sections.label: Acceptance
items: An external MCP client can discover and call your tools.
Comparison report on success, cost and latency; report the result even if multi-agent loses.
Memory expiry and retrieval covered by tests.
The same scenarios run on both frameworks; differences in control, debuggability and cost documented.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: MCP server, comparison report, memory design note.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: LLM threat model: direct and indirect prompt injection, data leakage, tool abuse.
Enforcing permissions at the retrieval and tool layer, not in the prompt.
PII handling, audit logging, OWASP LLM Top 10, NIST AI RMF vocabulary.

sections.label: Targets
items: Provable controls, not claimed ones.

sections.label: Implement
items: Field allowlists so the model sees only permitted data.
Row-level access filters in retrieval.
Red-team suite of about 40 attacks (including injection through retrieved documents and tool outputs) in CI.
PII detection and redaction.
Audit log schema: user, query, retrieved chunks, tool calls, model and prompt version, output.
Put the Python PII redactor and audit writer behind interfaces with contract tests and a benchmark harness; they become the reference implementations for later variants.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Security hardening of the KYC assistant with an attack report.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Prompt injection, data leakage, access control, guardrails, auditability (finance JD); data governance (AI-backend JD); adversarial inputs (security JDs).

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Cross-user and cross-tenant access tests all fail to leak data.
Red-team results documented, with residual risks listed honestly.
Any answer can be reconstructed from the audit log.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Red-team suite, audit schema, security design note.

weeks.title: Data pipeline, backtesting, first ML component

sections.label: Fundamental
items: CDC concepts (Debezium), event-driven feature pipelines.
Time-based splits, leakage, backtesting, shadow mode.
Baseline ML with scikit-learn; explaining results to business readers.

sections.label: Targets
items: Prove a model change with data before go-live; first step of the ML track.

sections.label: Implement
items: Postgres CDC to Kafka to a feature table.
Python anomaly or recommendation scorer (for example isolation forest) built with NumPy and pandas, with a time-split backtest.
Leakage tests; shadow deployment comparing the model against current behaviour.
Serve the scorer through a FastAPI REST service next to the gateway (Pydantic schemas, health checks) and expose it as a tool the agent can call.

Polyglot variant (about 5 hours): re-implement the Kafka consumer in Go (consumer groups, idempotent handler, retries, dead-letter queue) behind the same contract as the Python reference; benchmark both on the same replayed topic.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Transaction anomaly scoring for the KYC assistant, with a plain-language results memo.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Event-stream pipelines; backtests before go-live; classification and anomaly detection; explaining model results (AI-backend JD, security JD B); Go for high-throughput event consumers.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: A leakage test exists and passes.
Backtest compared against a naive baseline on a stated metric; if the model doesn't win, say so.
Memo is readable by a non-engineer.
The FastAPI endpoint has contract tests and a load-test baseline.
Go and Python consumers pass the same replay and poison-message tests; throughput, p99, memory and operational notes recorded; the Go variant is kept only if it clears the declared threshold.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Pipeline code, backtest notebook or script, one-page memo.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Spec-driven development with coding agents; review discipline; when not to trust generated code.
Architecture decision records (ADRs).

sections.label: Targets
items: Evidence of senior judgment and team-raising practices.

sections.label: Implement
items: Repo instruction file, test gates for agent-written code, a small internal tool or script that speeds your workflow (for example an eval-run command).
Five ADRs: model selection, retrieval design, agent workflow, cost and latency, permissions model.
"AI engineering standards" document: patterns, review checklist, eval requirements.
Choose one domain pack: finance KYC, payroll/HR, or security triage.

Polyglot variant (about 5 hours): Go edge gateway in front of the Python gateway (JWT or API-key auth, per-tenant rate limits and token budgets, SSE streaming proxy, audit events), compared with the same features in the Python gateway; write the ADR "Python vs Go at the edge".

sections.label: Practical project
items: Portfolio polish: README per repo, architecture diagrams, demo flow.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Daily use of AI coding tools with judgment (AI-backend JD); mentoring and reusable standards (finance JD).

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Each ADR lists alternatives and measured evidence.
Standards checklist applied to your own repo.
A written note of real cases where generated code was wrong or rejected (only real ones).
The edge ADR contains benchmark numbers (p95, throughput, memory) and a keep-or-retire decision; unauthorized and over-budget requests are rejected identically by both implementations.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: ADRs, standards document, polished repos, edge-gateway benchmark.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: AI system design; Python concurrency (asyncio, threads versus processes, the GIL); Kafka delivery and ordering; Postgres tuning; incident troubleshooting.

sections.label: Targets
items: Articulate trade-offs fluently; convert interviews into offers.

sections.label: Implement
items: Practise five design prompts aloud: KYC Q&A with audit; dispute-handling agent; halving cost and latency; injection defence for a tool-using agent; regression strategy when models change quarterly.
Three mock interviews; one timed coding exercise; one take-home simulation.
Story bank mapping every JD bullet to a concrete example with numbers.
Prepare two stories from the polyglot variants: one where Go or Rust won and one where Python was enough, each with numbers.
CV v2 tailored per JD; 10-15 applications plus referrals.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Five-minute capstone demo video and a one-page case study.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: All four JDs: decision-making, stakeholder communication, mentoring, incident handling.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Each design answer covers failure modes, evals, cost and security within 10 minutes.
Mock feedback captured and the top three gaps addressed.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Demo video, case study, story bank, application tracker.

weeks.title: Document AI I, OCR and layout analysis

sections.label: Fundamental
items: OCR pipeline: image preprocessing, text detection and recognition, digital-PDF text versus scanned pages.
Layout analysis: blocks, tables, reading order; layout-aware model families (LayoutLM-style) at concept level.
Metrics: character and word error rate, table-structure accuracy.

sections.label: Targets
items: Reliable text and structure from messy documents, with measured error.

sections.label: Implement
items: Pipeline with one open OCR engine (Tesseract, PaddleOCR or docTR; pick one) plus layout and table detection.
Router that sends digital PDFs and scanned pages down different paths.
Command-line tooling on Linux (poppler, ImageMagick) for batch processing.
Hand-label 50 pages to measure error rates.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Ingestion upgrade for the KYC assistant: scanned bank statements and invoices (synthetic or public datasets).

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Document AI: OCR, layout analysis; document pipelines feeding RAG.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Character and word error rates reported on 50 labelled pages.
Tables recovered with a measured structure score; failures catalogued.
Routing between digital and scanned paths tested.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Pipeline repo and an error-analysis report with failure examples.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Key-value and table extraction; LLM or VLM extraction versus layout-model extraction.
Confidence scoring, human-review routing, field-level evaluation, schema versioning.

sections.label: Targets
items: Extraction you can trust field by field, with a safe fallback.

sections.label: Implement
items: Schema-driven extraction (Pydantic) with an LLM or vision-language model, compared against a layout-based baseline.
FastAPI `/extract` service with typed request and response models, health checks and OpenAPI docs.
Confidence thresholds, review queue, PostgreSQL storage.
Field-level eval harness (exact and fuzzy match per field).

Polyglot variant (about 5 hours): Rust crate for document-text normalization and PII redaction, exposed to Python through PyO3 and benchmarked against the W7 Python reference on real OCR output; fuzz the parsing paths with `cargo-fuzz`.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Document intake service feeding the KYC assistant (statements, invoices).

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Information extraction; FastAPI and RESTful APIs; PostgreSQL; Rust for safe, fast handling of untrusted document text.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Per-field precision and recall reported; weakest fields identified.
Low-confidence results routed to review in tests.
Latency and cost per page recorded.
Rust and Python redactors produce identical detections on the labelled set; throughput and memory compared; fuzzing finds no crashes in a fixed budget (or each crash has a regression test).

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Deployed service and evaluation report.

weeks.title: Data and Python for ML (NumPy, Pandas)

sections.label: Fundamental
items: NumPy vectorization, pandas pipelines, exploratory analysis, statistics basics, leakage, metric selection.

sections.label: Targets
items: Fluent data wrangling; metrics tied to business cost.

sections.label: Implement
items: Cleaning and feature scripts; time-based train/validation/test splits.
Load the same dataset into PostgreSQL and MySQL; compare query plans, indexing and transaction behaviour.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Credit default or fraud dataset (public): full EDA with documented pitfalls.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: NumPy and pandas proficiency; PostgreSQL and MySQL; data skills for backtests.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Split strategy justified in writing; metric choice tied to cost; MySQL versus PostgreSQL differences documented with evidence.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: EDA report, reusable data-prep module, database comparison note.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Linear and logistic models, trees, regularization, cross-validation, calibration, class imbalance.
Random forest, gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM), search strategies for hyperparameters.

sections.label: Targets
items: Understand the models behind your scorers; know when tabular models beat LLMs.

sections.label: Implement
items: scikit-learn baselines; boosted models; Optuna search with proper validation; calibration curves; cost-based thresholds.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Fraud and credit-risk scorers integrated as agent tools; compare with the W8 baseline.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: ML fundamentals; hyperparameter tuning; model evaluation; classification and scoring.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Time-based backtest shows improvement over W8 or an honest tie; tuning budget and results logged; latency and cost per prediction recorded.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Models, backtest report, "LLM versus classical ML" decision note.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Isolation forest, one-class methods, seasonal baselines, forecasting basics, drift.

sections.label: Targets
items: Behavioural analytics usable by finance and security agents.

sections.label: Implement
items: Streaming-friendly detector, forecast baseline, drift checks, FastAPI endpoint.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Behaviour-baseline service: per-entity normal activity and deviation scores consumed by the agent.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Anomaly detection and behavioural pattern recognition.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: False-positive rate and detection delay measured on labelled or injected anomalies.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Service and evaluation report.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Tensors, autograd, training loops, optimizers, regularization, overfitting, learning-rate schedules, mixed precision.

sections.label: Targets
items: Write and debug a training loop without framework crutches.

sections.label: Implement
items: MLP for tabular data; CNN or sequence model on a small task; training scripts with seeds, configs and logged curves; GPU training run.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Alert or ticket classifier compared against the gradient-boosting baseline.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: PyTorch; deep learning understanding; model evaluation.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Reproducible training run; written comparison with the classical baseline, including cost and training time.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Training repo with seeds, configs and results.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Tokenization, embeddings, text classification, sequence labelling (NER), similarity search, reranker models.
TensorFlow/Keras model-building idioms versus PyTorch.

sections.label: Targets
items: Competent in both frameworks; evidence-based embedding choices.

sections.label: Implement
items: NER or classification model in PyTorch, ported to TensorFlow/Keras; compare effort, speed and results.
Embedding and cross-encoder reranker bake-off on your retrieval set.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Embedding and reranker bake-off for the policy corpus, feeding the winner back into the chassis.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: NLP; TensorFlow and PyTorch; semantic search and vector databases.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Report on recall, MRR, latency and cost per model; the chassis updated with the chosen model; TensorFlow port reproduces PyTorch metrics within a stated tolerance.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Bake-off report, updated retrieval module, both framework implementations.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Attention, positional encoding, KV cache, context-length cost, decoding strategies, training objectives.

sections.label: Targets
items: Reason about latency, memory and failure modes from first principles.

sections.label: Implement
items: Small GPT-style model on a toy corpus; measure memory and speed versus context length.
Read two foundational papers and summarise them in your own words.

sections.label: Practical project
items: "Why is this prompt slow and expensive?" analysis applied to your own agent traces.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Transformer architecture understanding; latency and token cost.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Written explanation links KV cache and context length to measured latency in your traces.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Mini-model repo and analysis note.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: When to fine-tune versus prompt versus retrieve; dataset curation and formatting; supervised fine-tuning (SFT); LoRA and PEFT mechanics; overfitting and forgetting.

sections.label: Targets
items: A first reproducible fine-tune evaluated on your own eval set.

sections.label: Implement
items: Curate 1,000+ examples for one narrow task (for example field extraction or case-note drafting).
SFT with LoRA on a small Qwen model using Hugging Face tooling; experiment tracking.
Evaluate against the prompted baseline on the same eval harness.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Fine-tuned extractor or drafter compared to the prompted baseline.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: LLM fine-tuning with LoRA, PEFT and SFT; model evaluation.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Training reproducible from config; quality, cost and latency compared with the prompted baseline; data-leakage check between train and eval sets.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Adapter, training config, comparison report.

weeks.title: Fine-tuning II, QLoRA and multi-model comparison

sections.label: Fundamental
items: QLoRA and 4-bit training; rank, alpha, learning-rate and batch-size effects; catastrophic forgetting; model selection across families.

sections.label: Targets
items: Hands-on evidence across Qwen, Llama and Mistral.

sections.label: Implement
items: QLoRA runs on Llama and Mistral models (plus the Qwen run from W19) with a hyperparameter search.
Evaluate quality, memory, speed and regression on general ability.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Three-model comparison on one task with a recommendation.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: QLoRA; Qwen, Llama and Mistral; hyperparameter tuning; model evaluation.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Table of quality, VRAM, training time and inference cost per model; recommendation justified; failures and instabilities documented.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Comparison report and reusable training templates.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: GPU architecture and memory hierarchy; CUDA execution model (kernels, threads, streams) at working level; profiling; mixed precision.
Quantization: GPTQ, AWQ, GGUF, bitsandbytes; accuracy versus speed trade-offs.

sections.label: Targets
items: Diagnose GPU bottlenecks and quantify quantization trade-offs. Scope: working literacy and profiling, not production kernel authoring.

sections.label: Implement
items: Profile training and inference with PyTorch profiler and Nsight basics.
Write one simple CUDA-level exercise (for example via Numba or Triton) to understand kernels.
Quantize one fine-tuned model with two methods; run evals on each.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Quantization study on the W19-20 model with quality, latency and memory results.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: GPU/CUDA, quantization, model optimization.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Bottleneck identified from a profile trace; quality loss per quantization method measured on your eval set.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Profiling notes and quantization report.

weeks.title: Serving and deployment, vLLM with FastAPI

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Serving engines, continuous batching, KV-cache memory, throughput versus latency, GPU containers, Linux operations, air-gapped packaging.

sections.label: Targets
items: Self-hosted models behind your existing gateway.

sections.label: Implement
items: Serve a model with vLLM (or an equivalent engine) and wrap domain endpoints in FastAPI.
Add an adapter to the gateway; run load tests; Dockerize with GPU support; operate the host with Linux tooling (systemd, logs, `nvidia-smi`, `perf`-style checks).
Offline packaging test for an air-gapped scenario.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Hosted versus self-hosted comparison on your eval set with a cost model.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: vLLM, FastAPI and REST deployment; Docker and Linux; on-premise deployments.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: The gateway switches to the local model by config; throughput, p95 latency and cost-per-request table produced; service restarts cleanly under failure tests.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Serving stack, load-test report, runbook.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Query rewriting, multi-hop retrieval, semantic layers, graph modelling (Neo4j basics), safe Text-to-SQL.

sections.label: Targets
items: Structured knowledge alongside documents.

sections.label: Implement
items: Read-only Text-to-SQL with schema allowlists and execution-accuracy evals.
Small entity graph for customers, accounts and cases.

sections.label: Practical project
items: "Ask your data" tool for the KYC assistant with query validation.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Text-to-Query, knowledge graphs, semantic layers.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Execution accuracy measured; destructive queries blocked by tests.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Text-to-Query module, graph prototype, evaluation report.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Experiment tracking (MLflow), model and prompt registries, canary and shadow releases, drift monitoring, rollback.
CI/CD on both GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

sections.label: Targets
items: Operate models and prompts like any production artifact, on either CI system.

sections.label: Implement
items: Track experiments and eval runs; register models, adapters and prompt versions; drift dashboards; canary release for a model change.
Mirror the pipeline in GitLab CI and note the differences (runners, caching, includes).

sections.label: Practical project
items: End-to-end release pipeline for the extractor, classifier and prompt set.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: MLOps/LLMOps; Git, Docker, CI/CD with GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: A deliberately bad model candidate is blocked by the gate; rollback tested; the same pipeline passes on both CI systems.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Pipeline definitions and runbook.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Model routing, caching layers, batching, streaming, budgets, distillation concepts.

sections.label: Targets
items: Reduce cost and latency without losing measured quality.

sections.label: Implement
items: Router sending easy requests to a cheaper or self-hosted model; permission-aware semantic and exact caches; per-tenant budget enforcement.
Polyglot variant (about 5 hours, optional): move exact-cache lookups and budget counters into the Go edge; compare end-to-end cost and p95 latency against the Python reference.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Cost-reduction exercise on the KYC assistant with before/after numbers.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Latency, cost and token efficiency.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: Documented cost and latency reduction with no regression on the eval gate.
Variant results recorded; if the edge version does not clear the threshold, retire it and note why.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Router, budget controls, results table.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Explainability methods, bias and fairness tests, model documentation, audit trails, regulatory vocabulary.

sections.label: Targets
items: Defend models to risk and compliance stakeholders.

sections.label: Implement
items: Explanations for the credit and fraud models; fairness slices; model cards; audit log extended to model decisions.
Polyglot variant (about 5 hours): Rust append-only audit store (idempotent writes, tamper-evident hashing, query endpoints) behind the same contract as the Python audit writer; load-test both.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Governance pack for the capstone: model cards, risk register, audit walkthrough.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: AI governance, model risk, explainability, KYC/AML.

sections.label: Acceptance
items: A non-technical reviewer can follow the audit walkthrough and find the evidence for a sample decision.
Rust and Python audit stores pass the same idempotency and reconstruction tests; write throughput, tail latency and memory compared.

sections.label: Deliverable
items: Governance pack.

sections.label: Fundamental
items: Platform design: reusable modules, versioned APIs, multi-product support, developer experience.

items: Turn the capstone into reusable capabilities.

Add a second domain pack to prove reuse.
Make every variant swappable by configuration against its Python reference; run one CI matrix across Python, Go and Rust with the same contract and eval tests.
Write a keep-or-retire ADR per variant using the benchmark results.

sections.label: Practical project
items: Second product built on the platform in a few days, with timing recorded.

sections.label: Production mapping
items: Shared AI platforms; reusable standards.
